Renovation Canvas is a spatial project workspace that connects renovation work, costs, problems, decisions, materials and evidence directly to the places they affect
The canvas is framed as a renovation workspace with spatial editing capabilities, not primarily a floor-plan editor with project-management features
Design principle: start with intent and add precision only when precision becomes valuable
The product's mental model maps WHERE+WHAT+WHAT NEXT to PROPERTY+CANVAS+CONTEXT INSPECTOR
The UI is organized into three panes -- Property, Canvas, Inspector -- each answering a distinct question: where am I, what is happening here, what should I do next
The core interaction loop is select context, capture intent, add information, refine when needed, execute/observe, update reality
The same interaction loop applies across both planning and execution
At the Conceptual fidelity level, no measurements or drawing are required; work, costs, photos, problems and decisions can already be attached
At the Approximate fidelity level, users position/resize spaces and establish approximate adjacency without needing accuracy

subject: At the Measured fidelity level, users calibrate or import plans, add dimensions, walls and openings, and define measurable zones so quantities can be derived
The system must never request precision without explaining the value of that precision
When precision is requested, the UI offers estimation-method options (rough estimate, use room area, measure on plan) with an explanation, instead of a bare imperative to calibrate
The initial canvas object vocabulary is deliberately small: Space, Work, Problem, Decision, Photo, Measurement
Cost begins as a property/refinement of Work rather than a standalone canvas object
A Space is meaningful physical context, such as a kitchen, bathroom, floor, garden or terrace
A Space's minimum required attributes are name, type and parent
A Space's optional attributes include geometry, area, dimensions, plan, status and budget
A Space can exist without geometry
Work describes a desired physical change, such as replace flooring, paint walls, move sink, replace windows, remove partition wall
Work creation is a simple flow: a description of what needs to happen plus an optional cost estimate
Advanced work information appears only through refinement, not at creation time
Problems are first-class objects because renovation reality frequently diverges from plan
The Problem inspector shows status, discovery date, photo count and cost impact, with actions to investigate or create work
A Problem's lifecycle is Observed, Investigating, Decision Needed, Work Created, Resolved
A Decision preserves alternatives and rationale, not just the chosen option
The Decision UI presents multiple options each with a cost, marks the selected option, and captures a reason
A Decision's lifecycle is Open, Evaluating, Decided, Superseded
A Decision must preserve what was decided, why, the alternatives considered, the impact, and when it was decided
Photos automatically inherit context: project, space, selected object and date
A Photo has an optional type: Before, During, After, Issue, Hidden Infrastructure, Receipt or Reference
Photos must remain evidence that stays understandable months or years later
Measurements are introduced only when needed for a quantity, layout or cost decision, not upfront
The UI must communicate why a measurement matters when requesting it
